jobs.title: Drift Wood #27 · December, still here
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, chin up, unkempt dark hair falling forward, sharp jaw; CHLOE — aged 18, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders. CHLOE wears u2 tee. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Last issue before break. Chloe's still here. It's the last December that's true. Panel 1: two teenagers walking down a small timber-town main street in December rain past a hardware store with half its Christmas lights dead, black and white (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE). Wood says "Where's Gully?". Chloe says "Crab bait. His uncle. He said it like it was a job.". Panel 2: a teenage girl walking and looking straight ahead down a rainy street, a boy beside her (in this panel: CHLOE). Chloe says "Applications are due in January. I sent four.". Wood says "Four is a lot of places to not be.". Panel 3: close-up of a teenage girl turning to ask a level question, rain on her hair (in this panel: CHLOE). Chloe says "How many did you send?". Panel 4: a rainy street corner at night, a girl walking away, a boy standing under a hardware store's Christmas lights as they all go out, black and white (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Wood says, in a small balloon, "...I'm working on the portfolio.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized crab, seen from above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
